raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Kimi K3 can lose or truncate non-streaming JSON content when a response-only answer quotes a think marker. This fix recognizes the actual response control tokens before searching the answer for reasoning markers, preserving the complete JSON and any following tool calls.

Supported workflow: non-streaming K3 output beginning with the response control prefix, through the unified parser used by Chat Completions and Responses. For example, `{"marker":"<|open|>think<|sep|>"}` currently produces reasoning `"}` and no content; the fix returns the original JSON in `content`.

## Claims

- Preserve JSON string values containing either a think opener or closer after the response control prefix.
- Keep ordinary text spelling a response opener in completed reasoning, including when the prompt already supplied the think opener.
- Reuse K3's existing content cleanup and tool extraction, without changing shared parser interfaces or streaming behavior.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New regressions on the frozen base | Three positive cases fail; the consumed-prefix reasoning control passes |
| K3 reasoning suite | 54 passed; no test-case skips |
| Related K3 reasoning and tool suites | 83 passed, including the 54 above; no test-case skips |
| Pinned official-tokenizer CPU comparison | Nine base failures corrected; four reasoning controls preserved, across 13 cases |
| Local HTTP/SDK replay | Six non-streaming requests: two base JSON failures corrected; the reasoning control preserved |
| Code quality | Applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy, passed |
| Independent review | Agent Bridge and two independent lanes found no introduced correctness or test-quality blocker |

The CPU comparison exercises native Chat and Responses parsing, plus automatic, required, named and disabled tool choice. It uses constructed token sequences, not model generation. The HTTP replay reuses the native Chat response generator and test fixtures through ASGI and the OpenAI SDK, with fixed engine outputs; all three candidate responses have the expected content, reasoning and completion-token usage.

<details>
<summary>Minimal CPU reproduction</summary>

Run in a dependency-prepared vLLM checkout. Only the pinned official tokenizer is loaded; no model weights are needed. Encode the response wrapper as control tokens and the JSON string as ordinary text.

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest
from vllm.parser.kimi_k3 import KimiK3Parser
from vllm.reasoning.kimi_k3_reasoning_parser import KimiK3ReasoningParser

class K3(KimiK3Parser):
    reasoning_parser_cls = KimiK3ReasoningParser

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(
    "moonshotai/Kimi-K3",
    revision="f831ab66814297da540d832a5235f8e904f29d06",
    trust_remote_code=True,
)
request = ChatCompletionRequest(model="kimi-k3", messages=[])
for marker in ("<|open|>think<|sep|>", "<|close|>think<|sep|>"):
    body = f'{{"marker":"{marker}"}}'
    ids = (tokenizer.encode("<|open|>response<|sep|>")
           + tokenizer.encode(body, allow_special_tokens=False))
    result = K3(tokenizer).parse(
        tokenizer.decode(ids), request, model_output_token_ids=ids,
    )
    print(result)
    assert result == (None, body, [])
```

Both assertions fail on base `29ae81fe` and pass with the fix. The tracked regressions also guard the inverse case: ordinary response-marker text inside reasoning must not become final content, and a tool call following the quoted-marker JSON must survive.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/reasoning/test_kimi_k3_reasoning_parser.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/parser/kimi_k3.py tests/reasoning/test_kimi_k3_reasoning_parser.py tests/tool_use/test_kimi_k3_tool_parser.py
```

</details>

## Details

The current K3 non-streaming extractor searches decoded text for think markers. Its response-only fallback runs only when neither think marker appears, so quoting one inside valid JSON defeats that fallback. A decoded response opener alone is not sufficient evidence of a channel transition: ordinary reasoning can spell the same characters.

The serving layer already passes generated token IDs to `KimiK3Parser.parse`. The fix checks only the leading response token sequence there, then uses the existing content cleanup and tool handoff. Other inputs retain the inherited path. The extra method stays local to K3; changing the shared reasoning-parser interface or migrating the parser engine is unnecessary. Calls without token IDs retain the pre-existing text-only behavior.

This investigation followed JSON failures in Moonshot AI's official [Kimi Vendor Verifier (KVV)](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-Vendor-Verifier). The endpoint's engine/version was unavailable. The reproduction establishes a vLLM source defect, not the cause of those endpoint failures.

With the streaming fix in [#60565](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60565) at `16bcdb5`, both quoted-marker JSON samples parse correctly when streamed, including one-token and whole-output delivery, but still fail in that revision's non-streaming path. This PR fixes the non-streaming path; streaming, grammar gating and token accounting are unchanged. The pre-existing handling of quoted response-close markers and text before the response opener remains outside this fix. Model inference and actual grammar-mask execution have not been exercised.

Related work: [#57098](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57098), [#57366](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57366) and [#50291](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50291) address truncated or markerless reasoning. Their inspected changes do not preserve JSON quoting think markers after a leading response control prefix. Source baseline: [29ae81fe](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/29ae81fe83712bb74c00a4ce0515d031f1225c9b). Rebased onto [a6b39f02](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/a6b39f02620e23422113823810148dfda9876304) with the production and test changes unchanged.

---

<details>
<summary>Pull Request Checklist</summary>

- [x] Used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill.
- [x] Design Fit: model-local change, existing helpers and interfaces retained.
- [x] Testing and Validation: CPU reproductions, targeted regressions and fixed-output serving replay pass; the tests use existing CI jobs.
- [x] Code Quality and Style: applicable lint/type checks pass; regressions use existing test helpers.
- [x] Pull Request Contents: problem, root cause, MRE and validation limits are included.

</details>

@@ -24,7 +24,7 @@
 RESPONSE_OPEN = f"{OPEN}response{SEP}"
 OPEN_IDS = [1, 2, 3]
 CLOSE_IDS = [4, 2, 3]
-RESPONSE_OPEN_IDS = [ord(ch) for ch in RESPONSE_OPEN]
+RESPONSE_OPEN_IDS = [1, 5, 3]
 
 
 class DummyTokenizer:
@@ -39,6 +39,8 @@ def encode(self, text: str, *args, **kwargs) -> list[int]:
             return [1, 2, 3]
         if text == THINK_CLOSE:
             return [4, 2, 3]
+        if text == RESPONSE_OPEN:
+            return RESPONSE_OPEN_IDS
         return [ord(ch) for ch in text]
 
 
@@ -107,6 +109,44 @@ def test_delegating_parser_strips_response_wrapper_without_tool_parser():
     assert tool_calls == []
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("marker", [THINK_OPEN, THINK_CLOSE])
+def test_response_only_json_preserves_quoted_think_marker(marker):
+    parser = ReasoningOnlyParser(_dummy_tokenizer())
+    request = ChatCompletionRequest(model="test-model", messages=[])
+    body = f'{{"marker":"{marker}"}}'
+
+    reasoning, content, tool_calls = parser.parse(
+        RESPONSE_OPEN + body,
+        request,
+        model_output_token_ids=[*RESPONSE_OPEN_IDS, *map(ord, body)],
+    )
+
+    assert reasoning is None
+    assert content == body
+    assert tool_calls == []
+
+
+def test_consumed_think_prefix_preserves_literal_response_marker():
+    parser = ReasoningOnlyParser(_dummy_tokenizer())
+    request = ChatCompletionRequest(model="test-model", messages=[])
+    reasoning = RESPONSE_OPEN + " is the response opener."
+    body = '{"ok":true}'
+    # The prompt already opened thinking. The generated opener below is ordinary
+    # text; only the later response opener is made of control tokens.
+    token_ids = [
+        *map(ord, reasoning),
+        *CLOSE_IDS,
+        *RESPONSE_OPEN_IDS,
+        *map(ord, body),
+    ]
+
+    assert parser.parse(
+        reasoning + THINK_CLOSE + RESPONSE_OPEN + body,
+        request,
+        model_output_token_ids=token_ids,
+    ) == (reasoning, body, [])
+
+
 def test_is_reasoning_end_uses_full_input_ids():
     parser = KimiK3ReasoningParser(DummyTokenizer())

@@ -177,6 +177,27 @@ def test_delegating_parser_preserves_tool_calls_after_reasoning():
     assert json.loads(tool_calls[0].arguments) == {"x": 1}
 
 
+def test_response_only_quoted_think_marker_preserves_tool_calls():
+    tokenizer = _dummy_tokenizer()
+    parser = KimiK3DelegatingParser(tokenizer)
+    body = f'{{"marker":"{THINK_CLOSE}"}}'
+    output = _response(body) + _tools(_call("calc", 1, _arg("x", "number", "1")))
+
+    reasoning, content, tool_calls = parser.parse(
+        output,
+        _request(),
+        enable_auto_tools=True,
+        model_output_token_ids=tokenizer.encode(output),
+    )
+
+    assert reasoning is None
+    assert content == body
+    assert tool_calls is not None
+    assert len(tool_calls) == 1
+    assert tool_calls[0].name == "calc"
+    assert json.loads(tool_calls[0].arguments) == {"x": 1}
+
+
 def test_delegating_parser_required_tool_choice_uses_xtml_parser():
     parser = KimiK3DelegatingParser(_dummy_tokenizer())
     request = _request().model_copy(update={"tool_choice": "required"})

@@ -25,6 +25,34 @@ class KimiK3Parser(DelegatingParser):
 
     # TODO: Switch Kimi K3 to the parser engine once its XTML reasoning/tool
     # path is covered there.
+    def parse(
+        self,
+        model_output: str,
+        request: ChatCompletionRequest | ResponsesRequest,
+        enable_auto_tools: bool = False,
+        model_output_token_ids: Sequence[int] = (),
+    ) -> tuple[str | None, str | None, list[FunctionCall] | None]:
+        reasoning_parser = self._reasoning_parser
+        if isinstance(reasoning_parser, KimiK3ReasoningParser):
+            response_open_ids = reasoning_parser._response_open_ids
+            if (
+                list(model_output_token_ids[: len(response_open_ids)])
+                == response_open_ids
+            ):
+                # A response control prefix wins over quoted think markers in
+                # its body. The same prefix as ordinary text is not a transition.
+                self._initialize_history_tool_call_cnt(request)
+                content = reasoning_parser._content_after_reasoning(
+                    model_output, request
+                )
+                tool_calls, content = self._extract_tool_calls(
+                    content, request, enable_auto_tools
+                )
+                return None, content, tool_calls
+        return super().parse(
+            model_output, request, enable_auto_tools, model_output_token_ids
+        )
+

         self,
         content: str | None,
